outputs.L3:
The method assesses how exposure to different colours of visible light affects a subject’s perception of tinnitus. A display is positioned within at least part of the subject’s field of view and illuminated by one or more variable light sources. During the assessment, measurable properties of the coloured light—such as wavelength, intensity, hue, saturation, or tristimulus values—are systematically varied while the subject monitors and reports any corresponding changes in tinnitus perception.

When the subject identifies a reduction, increase, or other alteration in perceived tinnitus, the relevant light values are recorded. These data can then be analysed to identify tristimulus values or other colour characteristics associated with alleviating tinnitus symptoms.

The approach further encompasses the generation of coloured-light data sets based on the recorded responses, as well as the subsequent use of those data sets to control or modify illumination within the subject’s visual field. It also includes related systems, apparatus, and articles configured to perform the assessment, store or process the resulting data, or deliver coloured light selected to reduce the subject’s perception of tinnitus.
outputs.L4:
The method evaluates the influence of visible-light colour on a person’s perception of tinnitus. During testing, controlled coloured light is presented across all or part of the subject’s visual field. Measurable illumination parameters—such as intensity, luminance, chromaticity, and tristimulus values—are varied systematically while the subject reports any change in the perceived loudness, pitch, character, or intrusiveness of the tinnitus. The responses are recorded and correlated with the light conditions present when an improvement, worsening, or other perceptual change occurs.

Repeated measurements can be used to identify colours and illumination levels associated with reduced tinnitus symptoms for a particular subject or group of subjects. The resulting information may be expressed as tristimulus coordinates or converted into specifications for producing the corresponding light. It may also be organized into data sets that relate selected colour values and intensities to reported tinnitus responses.

The identified parameters can then be applied through coloured-light sources, display systems, lamps, optical filters, tinted lenses, or similar devices capable of delivering the selected spectral and illumination characteristics. An apparatus for carrying out the method may include an adjustable light source, controls for varying and measuring colour and intensity, a viewing field or enclosure, a response-recording interface, and a processor for storing and analysing the collected data. In this way, the method provides an individualized, measurable basis for identifying visible-light conditions that may help alleviate or manage tinnitus symptoms.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for an invention that assesses and alleviates tinnitus by exposing a subject to variable colours of visible light and recording the colour values that alter tinnitus perception.
counterfactuals.output: A method and system for assessing and alleviating tinnitus are disclosed. A subject is exposed to a sequence of visible-light stimuli having variable colour values, including one or more of wavelength, hue, saturation, intensity, and temporal modulation. During or following each stimulus, an indication of the subject’s tinnitus perception is received and recorded, including a change in perceived loudness, pitch, location, character, or discomfort. The recorded indications are correlated with the respective colour values to identify one or more light settings associated with a reduction or other alteration of tinnitus perception. The identified settings may be stored as a subject-specific profile and subsequently reproduced in a therapeutic light-exposure protocol. The system may adaptively select further colour values based on prior responses and may monitor changes over repeated assessment or treatment sessions.

counterfactuals.prompt: Formulate broad intellectual-property language covering the testing and therapeutic use of variable coloured light for tinnitus relief.
counterfactuals.output:
Below is illustrative patent-style language intended as a drafting starting point, not a legal opinion on patentability, validity, or freedom to operate.

## Proposed Title

**Systems and Methods for Assessing and Treating Tinnitus Using Variable Spectral Light Stimulation**

## Broad Disclosure Language

Disclosed are systems, devices, and methods for evaluating, reducing, masking, modulating, or otherwise treating tinnitus by exposing a subject to light having a controllable optical characteristic. The optical characteristic may include wavelength, spectral composition, perceived color, intensity, luminance, irradiance, polarization, coherence, spatial distribution, temporal modulation, pulse duration, duty cycle, frequency, phase, presentation sequence, or any combination thereof.

In certain embodiments, one or more light-stimulation parameters are varied while a tinnitus-related response is obtained from the subject. The response may be subjective, behavioral, physiological, neurological, or any combination thereof. A stimulation parameter or treatment protocol may then be selected based at least partly on the response. Selected light stimulation may be administered in one or more sessions to reduce the perceived loudness, severity, intrusiveness, discomfort, frequency, duration, or other symptom or correlate of tinnitus.

Light may be presented to one or both eyes, to a portion of a visual field, through closed eyelids, or to another photosensitive tissue. Presentation may be continuous, intermittent, pulsed, patterned, sequenced, randomized, or adapted in real time. The light stimulation may be used alone or together with auditory, electrical, magnetic, tactile, vestibular, pharmaceutical, behavioral, or other therapeutic stimulation.

## Illustrative Claims

1. **A method of treating tinnitus in a subject, comprising:**  
   presenting light to the subject, the light having at least one controllable optical parameter;  
   varying the at least one controllable optical parameter among a plurality of parameter values;  
   identifying, based on a tinnitus-related response of the subject, at least one parameter value associated with a change in tinnitus; and  
   administering light according to a treatment protocol that includes the identified parameter value.

2. The method of claim 1, wherein the controllable optical parameter comprises wavelength, wavelength band, spectral power distribution, perceived color, intensity, luminance, irradiance, polarization, spatial pattern, temporal modulation, pulse frequency, pulse width, duty cycle, phase, duration, or a combination thereof.

3. The method of claim 1, wherein the tinnitus-related response comprises a reported change in tinnitus loudness, pitch, laterality, location, quality, annoyance, distress, masking, residual inhibition, or functional impact.

4. The method of claim 1, wherein the tinnitus-related response comprises a physiological or neurological measurement.

5. The method of claim 4, wherein the measurement comprises electroencephalography, evoked potential measurement, pupillometry, eye tracking, functional brain imaging, heart-rate variability, skin conductance, or an autonomic measurement.

6. The method of claim 1, wherein identifying the parameter value comprises comparing responses obtained during exposure to different colors or spectral distributions.

7. The method of claim 1, wherein the treatment protocol includes dynamically changing the optical parameter during a treatment session.

8. The method of claim 7, wherein the optical parameter is changed according to a predetermined sequence, a pseudorandom sequence, a subject-selected sequence, or a feedback-control algorithm.

9. The method of claim 1, wherein the light is presented monocularly, binocularly, asymmetrically to the subject’s eyes, through one or both closed eyelids, or within a selected portion of the subject’s visual field.

10. The method of claim 1, further comprising presenting auditory stimulation coordinated with the light.

11. The method of claim 10, wherein the auditory stimulation is selected according to a tinnitus pitch, hearing profile, or response to the light.

12. The method of claim 1, wherein the treatment protocol is modified during or after administration based on a further tinnitus-related response.

13. The method of claim 1, wherein administration produces a therapeutic effect during light presentation or for a period following light presentation.

14. The method of claim 1, wherein the subject has subjective tinnitus, objective tinnitus, unilateral tinnitus, bilateral tinnitus, tonal tinnitus, pulsatile tinnitus, intermittent tinnitus, or chronic tinnitus.

15. **A method of assessing tinnitus, comprising:**  
   exposing a subject to each of a plurality of light stimuli differing in at least one optical parameter;  
   receiving, for each light stimulus, data indicative of a tinnitus-related response; and  
   generating, from the data, a subject-specific light-response profile.

16. The method of claim 15, further comprising selecting or generating a tinnitus-treatment protocol from the subject-specific light-response profile.

17. The method of claim 15, wherein the plurality of light stimuli is selected adaptively in response to previously received tinnitus-related responses.

18. The method of claim 15, further comprising storing the subject-specific light-response profile and using the profile to monitor tinnitus or treatment efficacy over time.

19. **A system for assessment or treatment of tinnitus, comprising:**  
   a light-emitting assembly configured to present light having an adjustable spectral characteristic;  
   an input interface configured to receive data indicative of a tinnitus-related response; and  
   a controller configured to vary the adjustable spectral characteristic, associate the tinnitus-related response with the presented light, and generate or administer a subject-specific light-stimulation protocol.

20. The system of claim 19, wherein the light-emitting assembly comprises one or more light-emitting diodes, displays, lamps, lasers, tunable optical sources, optical filters, head-mounted displays, eyewear devices, goggles, contact-lens devices, mobile-device displays, or room-lighting devices.

21. The system of claim 19, wherein the controller implements closed-loop control that changes the light in response to the tinnitus-related response.

22. The system of claim 19, further comprising a sensor configured to obtain physiological or neurological data from the subject.

23. The system of claim 19, further comprising an audio transducer, electrical stimulator, tactile actuator, or magnetic-stimulation device operated in coordination with the light-emitting assembly.

24. **A non-transitory computer-readable medium** storing instructions that, when executed by one or more processors, cause a system to:  
   control presentation of a plurality of spectrally distinct light stimuli to a subject;  
   obtain tinnitus-related response data;  
   determine a light-stimulation parameter associated with improvement in tinnitus; and  
   control subsequent presentation of light using the determined parameter.

## Useful Definition

As used herein, “treating tinnitus” includes curing, alleviating, suppressing, masking, reducing, interrupting, modulating, preventing worsening of, improving tolerance of, or reducing one or more perceptual, emotional, neurological, behavioral, or functional effects associated with tinnitus. “Colored light” includes light defined by perceived color or by any spectral property, including narrowband, broadband, monochromatic, polychromatic, metameric, visible, near-ultraviolet, or near-infrared light, whether or not consciously perceived as color.
